conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital tonight?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I went to dialysis this morning and afterward I started feeling really unwell—nauseous, chills, and a bit feverish. I didn’t vomit, but I just didn’t feel right.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, none of that. My graft site feels okay—no pain or drainage. Same with my catheter.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. You had a fever in the ER—99.7—and your white blood cell count was a bit high. We’re going to run some tests to check for infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Could this be related to the antibiotics I got last time? I had a bad reaction before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know about your allergy to cefazolin and penicillins. You didn’t get any antibiotics today, so this is likely something else. We’ll keep that in mind.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I’m just worried because I’ve been through a lot with my kidneys and heart.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. We’ll take good care of you. Let me check your mouth quickly—sometimes infections can show up there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see some white patches in your mouth. That looks like thrush—a fungal infection. It’s common in people on dialysis, especially after antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thrush? I’ve never had that. Is it serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not usually. It’s treatable with a mouth rinse. We’ll start you on nystatin. It’s important we rule out any deeper infection, like in the esophagus, but you’re not having trouble swallowing, so that’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I can swallow fine. So this could be why I feel so off?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. The fever and chills could be from the thrush, especially since we don’t see signs of bacterial infection. Your blood cultures and chest X-ray are being checked now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. What about my heart? I had that chest X-ray—did it show anything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The X-ray shows some subtle fluid in the lungs, but given your history, it’s likely mild and not from heart failure. We’ll monitor your weight and breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. I’ve had a lot of heart issues—the blocked arteries, stents. I worry every time I feel unwell.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see you’ve had a stent placed in the RCA after rotablation. Your troponin was slightly elevated, but it’s stable. We don’t think this is a heart attack.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. That’s a relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your blood cultures came back negative—no bacteria grew. Urine culture showed contamination, so we’re not concerned about a UTI.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No bacterial infection. We think the fever and chills were due to the thrush. Since you’re feeling better and afebrile, we’ll stop the IV antibiotics we started yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I’m still on the nystatin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for 14 days. Use it four times a day. It’s important to finish the whole course even if your mouth looks better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Can I still go to dialysis tomorrow?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re scheduled for hemodialysis tomorrow at noon. Your AV graft is doing well—good thrill and no signs of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’m glad that thrombectomy last week helped.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the graft is functioning. Once it’s fully ready, we’ll remove the tunneled catheter. That’ll lower your infection risk.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You just finished dialysis. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Much better. No nausea or chills. I think I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow morning. You’ve stayed afebrile, and all signs point to improvement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need any follow-up tests?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just continue your regular dialysis schedule. If you develop trouble swallowing or chest pain when eating, let your doctor know—we might need to consider fluconazole instead.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my other meds—should I keep taking them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your usual medications—sevelamer, aspirin, clopidogrel, metoprolol, the rest. We’re not changing anything else.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the nystatin? Any side effects?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s very safe. Some people get mild stomach upset, but it’s rare. Just swish and swallow four times a day with meals and at bedtime.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re cleared to go home. We’ll arrange transportation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better. Just one thing—should I watch my weight?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, weigh yourself every morning. Call your doctor if you gain more than three pounds in a day—that could mean fluid buildup.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. And if my mouth gets worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you have pain when swallowing, call your nephrologist. They may switch you to a pill form of antifungal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. Thanks for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up as needed.
